title: The greenhouse effect
body:
A planet's surface temperature depends on far more than its distance from the Sun. A thick atmosphere of gases like carbon dioxide lets sunlight in but traps the heat trying to escape — the greenhouse effect.

Venus is the classic example: a dense CO₂ atmosphere makes it the hottest planet (about 465°C), even though Mercury orbits closer to the Sun.

example.question: Why is Venus hotter than Mercury despite being farther from the Sun?
steps: Mercury is closer, so it receives more sunlight.
But Mercury has almost no atmosphere, so its heat escapes to space.
Venus's thick CO₂ atmosphere traps heat — a runaway greenhouse effect.
example.answer: Venus's dense CO₂ atmosphere traps the heat.

commonMistakes: Assuming the planet closest to the Sun must be the hottest — atmosphere matters more than distance.
